_source: Watched in the owner's Chrome 2026-11-17: frames every ~5 s to 65 s, words from YouTube's transcript panel (full). Our own descriptions; shots approximate from sampled frames.

hook.firstFrame: a muted vintage map of North America with a small ship and a French flag
hook.firstLine: The US sent two diplomats to buy one city and bought a territory instead.

shots.picture: vintage map of North America, a ship crossing toward France
two big-headed cartoon diplomats meeting a cartoon Napoleon over a map of France
the leaders shaking hands over a map of Western Europe
France and Britain coloured red and blue on the map, a truce
cartoon Napoleon dreaming, a thought bubble of the American empire
a 3D globe swinging to the Caribbean, North America recoloured by owner
the island of Haiti with fire markers across its plantations
a cartoon worker standing in a sugar field
Haiti turns blue as control is lost
a French warship sailing past the island
the island alone in dark blue after the army is lost
a cut-out portrait of Napoleon beside North America coloured by territory
the Mississippi and New Orleans highlighted, Jefferson's offer
Louisiana recoloured as American, the country doubling on the map

lines.gist: set out to buy one city, bought the whole territory for about the same price
a peace in Europe that both sides knew was short
Napoleon's American plan rested on his richest colony
the colony's revolution and a disease destroyed his army there
without it the territory was useless; America wanted the river port
he offered everything; the country doubled in a day at a few cents an acre

ending.lastFrame: North America with the purchase recoloured

whyItWorks: a paradox in the first sentence: set out to buy a city, came home with half a continent
a chain of causes, each shown as the map changing colour
historical figures as cartoon characters reacting, with one real portrait
the most surprising figure (cents an acre) saved for the last line
